mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains > 5.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.1) during the identified tightening window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.7%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations, which elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the identified inflation acceleration episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (labor supply) creates a dual-pressure labor market that raises corporate earnings expectations and compresses wage growth, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified labor market tightness episode (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 2% for three consecutive months signals weakening demand momentum, which reduces equity risk appetite and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥ 2% monthly for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the identified demand slowdown period.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% in a month relative to the prior month, it indicates supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and elevates equity volatility, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or are only marginally negative (p > 0.15) during the identified contraction episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) above 110% for two consecutive months signals excess liquidity in the financial system, which lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses above 110% and remains > 110% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during the liquidity expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where UNRATE falls below 4% and HOUST (household utilization) remains above 80% for two consecutive months, the dual labor market slack condition reduces recession risk and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND HOUST > 80% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during the identified labor market slack episode.

mechanism_narrative: When a sharp one-month drop in HOUST (household utilization) of at least 6 percentage points coincides with a decline in INDPRO of more than 3%, it reflects simultaneous demand and supply softening, which amplifies market uncertainty and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥ 6 pp in a month AND INDPRO decreases by > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or are only marginally negative (p > 0.15) during the identified softening episode.
